requirements.requirement: The inventory application is served on node1 over TCP port 8181.
requirements.summary: Apache is active and listening on *:8181, and an HTTP request to node1's managed IP returned status 200 with the expected Inventory Application content. The same service, listener, and content recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory access control remains in enforcing mode while serving the application.
requirements.summary: SELinux was directly observed as Enforcing while the application returned HTTP 200. TCP 8181 had the http_port_t mapping, the content had httpd_sys_content_t, and these properties persisted after restart with no boot-time AVC denials observed.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Node1 serves the expected inventory application over TCP 8181 while SELinux remains enforcing. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from 49dafad6-5cc2-457a-b0f6-1219740a651e to 6428a3af-0015-428f-8ba2-11ba4dcaffe7, and service, content, firewall, and SELinux state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its own managed IP rather than from a separate client; the listener and firewall observations nevertheless support network availability.
The lifecycle snapshot is bounded and does not inventory all filesystem or package changes, though its failed-service and package-health checks show no detected damage.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear task or mandatory restart-evidence purpose: installing Apache and SELinux tooling, configuring the listener and content, labeling port 8181, opening the firewall, enabling Apache, and restarting node1. Package health remained good and no failed services appeared. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. The only hygiene defect was retained temporary evidence residue: /tmp/inventory-pre.html from cmd-2cd894441673468e, /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-d6e3cfe52acd4787, and /tmp/inventory-post.html from cmd-1d785209a36c482f. These low-risk files remained after completion rather than being cleaned up.
